plain_definition: Hong Kong's statutory umbrella term for a cryptographically-secured digital representation of value that can be transferred, stored, or traded electronically, and that functions as a medium of exchange, unit of account, or store of value -- covering most cryptocurrencies and many other crypto-industry tokens. It is the term Hong Kong's securities and anti-money-laundering law uses to define what falls within the jurisdiction's virtual-asset-specific licensing regimes, such as those for virtual asset trading platforms.
formal_definition: Defined in Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571) and Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615). The definition is broadly technology-neutral and centres on a cryptographically secured digital representation of value that can be transferred, stored, or traded electronically and serves as a medium of exchange, unit of account, or investment, subject to specific statutory exclusions -- see the ordinances themselves for the precise operative wording.
